text: I purchased Order 42, and it arrived with a cracked casing — clearly damaged before it ever reached me. I paid for an intact, working product, not something broken out of the box. I'm asking for a full refund.

Order 42 was dispatched in perfect condition and delivered exactly as specified, so the damage clearly occurred after it was in the claimant's hands. I have dispatch photos and delivery confirmation to back that up, and I'm happy to submit them to the arbitrator. Since the item was accepted intact at delivery, I can't accept responsibility for what happened afterward and must decline the refund.

Your dispatch photos show the item's condition at packing, not what it survived in transit, and a delivery confirmation only proves the box arrived — the crack was there the moment I opened it. I welcome the ruling that this falls under the refund rule, and I expect the full refund to be processed promptly.
